solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unproductive lawyers' fee falling short

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers

indicators.note: falling short says the word for the fee stops before its final letter

parts.note: rent is a fee paid for the use of property

explanation.surface: A complaint that the legal profession's charges are getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' drops the T from RENT, leaving REN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: barren land or a barren effort yields nothing.

clue.text: Perplex politician with an empty store of money?

parts.note: CON is short for a Conservative politician

indicators.note: with is read as 'containing': the store of money holds the zero inside it

parts.note: a fund is a store of money set aside
an empty thing is nothing, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a politician presiding over an empty treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' places O within FUND to give FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to confound someone is to baffle them.

clue.text: Criminal oafs without fear getting one in an uncomfortable situation

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Fearless criminal louts land somewhere they do not belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a container signal but is simply part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone ill at ease in unfamiliar surroundings is said to be like that stranded creature.

clue.text: Doubt possibly about King beginning to emerge and become prominent

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the royal letter
possibly signals that the letters of the word doubt might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Uncertainty surrounding a monarch who starts to come forward and make his mark.
explanation.walkthrough: OBTUD (DOUBT rearranged) goes round R, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense: to obtrude is to stick out or push forward into notice.

clue.text: One determining roles caught by a deception with inspector and minister

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a sting is a confidence trick
DI is a Detective Inspector
a rector is a parish minister

explanation.surface: A con involving a police officer and a clergyman, like a crime drama plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this film or theatre professional chooses which actors play each part.

clue.text: Evoke priest with short name

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: short means the verb for naming loses its final letter

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A cleric with a brief title summoning up memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CITE to CIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to elicit a response is to draw it out or call it forth.

clue.text: Endless jar producing smile

indicators.note: endless says the verb for jarring loses its last letter

parts.note: to grind is to grate or jar harshly

explanation.surface: Something about a never-ending jar of drink raises a smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a container or a drink but is a verb meaning grate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a broad facial expression of amusement, noun to noun.

clue.text: Proper conduct having taken in cold food abroad

indicators.note: having taken in shows the word for proper conduct swallowing the abbreviation

parts.note: the Tao in Chinese philosophy is the Way, the right path of conduct
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Good manners when eating cold dishes overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a folded Mexican tortilla with filling is a foreign dish.

clue.text: Fellow in the same place producing pork pie

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
IB is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place

explanation.surface: A man found at the same spot making a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang (often shortened to porky) for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: a porky is a small untruth.

clue.text: Enticement in a liberal law after switching sides

indicators.note: sides are right and left, R and L, which change places in the word for law

parts.note: a rule is a law or regulation

explanation.surface: A lenient statute that changes its political stance becomes tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' are right and left, whose abbreviations R and L trade places; politics is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: charm or attraction that draws someone in.

clue.text: Earnings largely cut by paper in which setters are exhibited?

indicators.note: cut by shows the newspaper slicing into the shortened word
largely means most of the word, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: a crust is a living, as in earning a crust
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Wages trimmed by a newspaper, with a wry nod to crossword compilers.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUS (CRUST shortened) is cut by FT. Setters are the dogs, not compilers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the famous annual British dog show where breeds such as Irish setters compete.

clue.text: Uncommunicative cretin stupidly holding electronic timetable's cover

indicators.note: holding shows the rearranged letters wrapping round the next pieces
stupidly suggests the letters of cretin are put in a foolish order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: cover is the front of the timetable, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fool absurdly clutching the front of an online schedule says nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: RICENT, from 'cretin' rearranged, holds ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a reticent person keeps thoughts to themselves.

clue.text: Militant unionist in road getting round ban without a new challenge to authority?

indicators.note: getting round shows the rearranged letters enclosing what is left of the ban
militant suggests disruption, so these letters are thrown into a new order
without means the following letters are taken out of the word ban

explanation.surface: A hardline trade unionist on the road, flouting a ban: a picket line scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Militant' reads as an adjective for the unionist but is the anagram signal; 'without' is a deletion, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: defiance of superiors, refusing orders, defies authority; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Game fellow abandoned wise sort

indicators.note: abandoned says the fellow's letter has left the game birds

parts.note: fowl are game birds

explanation.surface: A sporting chap walks out on a shrewd character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is the noun for hunted birds, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition: the bird is a symbol of wisdom, associated with Athena.

clue.text: Charge girlfriend?

definitions.meaning: an official commission or instruction to act
read as two words, a bloke's evening companion: the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,4, the answer is a date for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for the first sense; the second is a playful split into two words.

clue.text: Regular features in Cold War promoted trouble

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means moved up, so the letters read from bottom to top
regular features are every other letter of the phrase, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Superpower tensions stirring up conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters O, D, A are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Eccentric comedian missing first part of a game?

indicators.note: missing first means the comedian's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a British comedian from Knotty Ash in Liverpool
a ball is the object used in many games

explanation.surface: A quirky comic who skips the opening of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a famous British stand-up comedian; drop his D to get ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a strange or unconventional person or way.

clue.text: Sprinter restored to health, we hear, in secluded place

parts.note: Usain Bolt is the Jamaican sprinter

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: whole in its old sense of healed or sound in body

explanation.surface: A runner, back on his feet, hiding away somewhere quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: WHOLE (healed) sounds like HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a refuge or hideaway where one can escape notice.

clue.text: Impressionist's art found in operatic character with contralto really pouring out heart?

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme

indicators.note: pouring out heart means the middle of really is emptied, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: An opera heroine's emotional aria, sung by a contralto with feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' is a mimic, not a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a comic impressionist's skill is imitating others.

clue.text: Frock with garb tailor altered in territory overseas

indicators.note: altered, as a tailor alters clothes, means these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A dress and outfit that a tailor modified abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British Overseas Territory at the southern tip of Spain.

clue.text: Fibre that's not good I removed in short low vehicle

indicators.note: in places the shortened wickedness inside the shortened vehicle
short means the racing vehicle loses its last letter

parts.note: a kart is a low racing vehicle, a go-kart

indicators.note: removed says the letter I is taken out of the word for wickedness

parts.note: evil means bad, not good

explanation.surface: Seemingly about a poor-quality material taken out of a low-slung car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link; 'short' trims the go-kart's final letter and 'removed' strips the I from wickedness before the two are nested.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a strong synthetic material used in body armour.

clue.text: A university concealed by neat courtyard

indicators.note: concealed by shows the tidy word hiding the university letter

parts.note: trim means neat or tidy

explanation.surface: A college tucked away behind a tidy quad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an open central court within a building.

clue.text: Person consuming very similar restricted foreign fare

indicators.note: consuming means the person swallows the abbreviation

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in not a soul

indicators.note: restricted means the word for similar is cut short at its end

parts.note: akin means similar

explanation.surface: Someone eating a restricted diet of nearly identical dishes abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUL eats V, then AKIN loses N.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Greek kebabs of grilled meat on skewers count as fare from overseas.

clue.text: Stretch of romantic country with a lot of desert

definitions.text: country with a lot of desert

indicators.note: stretch of means a run of letters taken from within the word romantic

explanation.surface: A dreamy landscape of sand dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: the Arabian sultanate is largely arid sandy terrain.

clue.text: Group of individuals in house right to enter short function

indicators.note: to enter puts the house and right letters inside the abbreviated function

parts.note: cot is the short form of cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A household where something is cut short, a math lesson perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a band of people sharing a characteristic, like a year's intake.

clue.text: March is not seen in blissful state

indicators.note: not seen in means the letters of the little word vanish from the blissful state

parts.note: paradise is a state of perfect happiness

explanation.surface: Spring in heaven goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is the verb or noun for a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a procession or marching display.

clue.text: Foreign character accommodated in superior hotel

indicators.note: accommodated in says the letters lodge inside the words superior hotel

explanation.surface: An exotic guest staying at a luxury hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Lecturer dismissed aggressive youth

parts.note: out means dismissed, as a batsman is in cricket

explanation.surface: A teacher sacked because of a hooligan student.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a yob or uncouth young man.
